Rashi on Niddah 13b:10:1.english: And won't his belly be split open - Due to the thorn.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:11:1.hebrew: למטה מטבורו - והכי קאמר: תקצץ על שהכניסה למטה מטבורו:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:11:1.english: Below his navel - And this is what he is saying: [His hand] should be severed for having inserted it below his navel.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:13:1.english: And show her - For she was expert in the appearance of impure blood and pure blood.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:14:1.hebrew: מדברת ואינה שומעת - כבר שמעה ולמדה לדבר, ואחר כן נתחרשה:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:14:1.english: [A woman who] speaks but does not hear - She had already heard and learned to speak, and afterward she became deaf.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:14:2.english: Everywhere - To exclude [him] from the category of a person of sound mind.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:17:1.english: That he does not sleep - So that he does not become heated and experience [a seminal emission].

Rashi on Niddah 13b:18:1.english: A leather pouch - And when they want to feed him [teruma], they will check the pouch.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:19:1.hebrew: ותבלע בכיס - וקאכיל תרומה בטומאת הגוף, והוי במיתה, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:ט׳) ומתו בו כי יחללוהו:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:19:1.english: And it is swallowed in the pouch - And he is eating teruma in bodily impurity, and it is punishable by death, as it is written (Leviticus 22:9): "and die thereby if they profane it."

Rashi on Niddah 13b:1:1.english: From the corona and above - Toward the body.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:21:1.hebrew: רואין אותן - לענין מי חטאת קאמר, לטמא במשא, דבעי' עד דדרי כשיעור הזאה, כדאמר בפ"ק (לעיל נדה ט.): כמה יהו במים ויהיה בהם כדי הזאה? כדי שיטבול ראשי גבעולין ויזה. כלומר, כדי שיהא בהם כדי להזות, לבד מה שהאזוב בולע:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:21:1.english: One considers them - He is speaking with regard to the purification water, [concerning its ability] to transmit impurity through carrying, for we require that one carry [at least] the measure of a sprinkling, as it says in the first chapter (above, Niddah 9a): "How much must there be in the water for there to be enough for a sprinkling? Enough so that one may dip the tips of the stalks and sprinkle." That is to say, so that there will be enough in it to sprinkle, aside from what the hyssop absorbs.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:21:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda says, etc., of copper - Evidently, [an object made] of copper does not absorb.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:22:1.hebrew: שמע מינה - מדקתני כל שכן שאתה מביאו לידי חימום, אלמא מכנסים אסורין:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:22:1.english: Learn from this - From the fact that [the baraita] teaches: "All the more so that you bring him to warming," it follows that trousers are forbidden.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:23:1.hebrew: פמלניא - סינר, פורצינ"ט. חללו תלוי למטה ברוחב, שלא יתעטף האבר ויתחמם:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:23:1.english: Pamalanya - An apron [Old French: porceint]. Its interior hangs down loosely in width, so that the organ does not become wrapped and heated.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:23:2.hebrew: של פרושים - צנועים. ל"א: של פרשים:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:23:2.english: Of the abstinent - Modest [people]. Another version: Of horsemen.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:23:3.english: Straps - [In Old French:] laces, similar to ours.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:23:4.hebrew: ואין להם לא בית הנקב ולא בית הערוה - כלומר, חללו רחב ותלוי למטה, ולא היה תיק בין הירכיים להיות האבר מתעטף בו, שלא יבא (האבר) לידי הרהור, והיינו בית הערוה. ובית הנקב: כשהן קצרות כנגד נקב הרעי כתבנית אדם, נכנסות בין עגבותיו ומלוכלכות בזיעה, וגנאי הוא לבגדי קדש בכך. לישנא אחרינא: בית הנקב ובית הערוה — דרכן היה לעשות נקבים במכנסים כנגד בית הערוה להשתין מים לחוץ דרך שם, וכן כנגד בית הרעי, וכשגומר, קושר הנקב ברצועה וסותמו:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:23:4.english: And they have neither a place for the orifice nor a place for the nakedness - That is to say, its interior was wide and hung down low, and there was no pouch between the thighs for the organ to be enveloped in, so that (the organ) would not come to [arousal from impure] thoughts; and this is [what is meant by] "a place for the nakedness." And [as for] "a place for the orifice": When [trousers] are tight-fitting opposite the orifice of excrement according to the human form, they enter between his buttocks and become soiled with sweat, and that is a disgrace for sacred vestments. Another explanation: [Regarding] "a place for the orifice and a place for the nakedness" — it was their practice to make openings in trousers opposite the genitalia to urinate outward through there, and similarly opposite the place of excrement; and when one finishes, one ties the opening with a strap and closes it.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:3:1.english: And it was evil - It follows that he is called evil.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:3:2.english: And it is written: "Shall not sojourn with You" - Evil shall not sojourn with You.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:4:1.english: With the hand - One who emits semen in vain.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:5:1.hebrew: כספחת - דכתיב בגרים (ישעיהו יד): ונלוה הגר עליהם ונספחו על בית יעקב, לשון ספחת. שקשים לישראל כספחת, שאין בקיאים במצות ומביאין פורענות, ועוד שמא למדים ישראל ממעשיהן, מפי מורי הזקן. ויש אומר: שכל ישראל ערבים זה בזה. ולאו מילתא היא, שלא נתערבו בשביל הגרים, דאמרינן במס' סוטה (דף לז:): נמצא לכל אחד מישראל שש מאות אלף ושלשת אלפים ותק"ן בריתות שכולן נתערבו זה בזה, אלמא לא נתערבו על הגרים:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:5:1.english: As a scab - For it is written concerning converts (Isaiah 14): "And the stranger shall join them, and they shall attach to the house of Jacob" — an expression of sapachat [scab]. [And the reason] that they are as difficult for Israel as a scab is that they are not proficient in the mitzvot and bring retribution, and furthermore, lest Israel learn from their deeds — [this explanation is] from the mouth of my teacher the Elder. And there is [one] who says: Because all of Israel are guarantors for one another. But this is not correct, for they did not become guarantors on behalf of converts, as we say in Tractate Sotah (page 37b): "It is found for each member of Israel [that there are] six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty covenants, in all of which they became guarantors for one another." Hence, they did not become guarantors for converts.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:6:1.hebrew: בני סקילה נינהו - ואת אמרת מעכבים את המשיח, ותו לא? הלא במיתה הן נידונים:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:6:1.english: They are liable to stoning - And you say [that] they delay the Messiah, and nothing more? Behold, they are sentenced to death!

Rashi on Niddah 13b:6:2.hebrew: דרך אברים - היינו שכבת זרע לבטלה, ואינו משכב זכור, דבמשכב זכור כתיב (ויקרא כ) משכבי אשה:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:6:2.english: By way of limbs - That is, emission of semen in vain, and it is not male intercourse, for regarding male intercourse it is written (Leviticus 20): "as with a woman."

Rashi on Niddah 13b:7:1.hebrew: דנסיבי קטנות - והוא ראוי להוליד, נמצא בטל מפריה ורביה כל ימי קטנותה:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:7:1.english: That they marry minor girls - And he is capable of fathering children, [so] he turns out to be neglecting [the mitzvah of] procreation all the days of her minority.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:7:2.english: That are in the Guf - A chamber, for Guf is the name of the place designated for the souls that are destined to be born.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:7:3.hebrew: כי רוח - הרוחות שלפני, שגזרתי להיות נולדים קודם. יעטוף - מעכב את הגאולה, דקרא בגאולה כתיב: כי לא לעולם אריב ולא לנצח אקצוף וגו'. נשמות שאני עשיתי יעטוף, ומסיפיה לרישיה מדריש. יעטוף - כמו (בראשית ל) והעטופים ללבן:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:7:3.english: For the spirit - The spirits that are before Me, which I decreed should be born first. "Ya'atof" [means that it] delays the redemption, for the verse is written concerning the redemption: "For I will not contend forever, neither will I be always wroth, etc." [The phrase] "the souls that I have made" [connects to] "ya'atof" [delays], and it is expounded from its end to its beginning. "Ya'atof" is like (Genesis 30): "And the late-born belonged to Laban."

Rashi on Niddah 13b:8:1.hebrew: קץ ידא - דאמרינן בסנהדרין: כל המרים ידו על חבירו תקצץ, דכתיב: וזרוע רמה תשבר. רב הונא קץ ידא, אלמא תקצץ דינא הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:8:1.english: Severed a hand - For we say in Sanhedrin [58b]: Anyone who raises his hand against his fellow, [his hand] should be severed, as it is written: "And the high arm shall be broken" (Job 38:15). Rav Huna severed a hand — evidently, "[his hand] should be severed" is a legal penalty.

Rashi on Niddah 13b:9:1.hebrew: תקצץ ידו על טבורו - קס"ד טבורו ממש, והיינו דאמרי ליה: והלא כריסו נבקעת, כשקוצצין שם את ידו:
Rashi on Niddah 13b:9:1.english: His hand should be severed upon his navel - [The Gemara] initially thought [that this means] literally upon his navel, and that is why they said to him: "Won't his belly be split open?" — when they sever his hand there.

Tosafot on Niddah 13b:10:1.hebrew: דינא תנן - ובשבת (דף קח:) דאמרי' יד לפה תקצץ, אינו לא דינא ולא לטותא; אלא כלומר: טוב לו לקוץ ידו קודם שיגע למקומות הללו משום בת מלך:
Tosafot on Niddah 13b:10:1.english: Do we learn [it as] a judicial penalty? - And in Shabbat (108b), where we say: "[A] hand to the mouth should be severed," it is neither a judicial penalty nor a curse; rather, [it is] as if to say: It would be better for him to sever his hand before he touches these places, on account of Bat Melekh [the harmful spirit that rests on unwashed hands in the morning].

Tosafot on Niddah 13b:10:2.hebrew: אלמא דינא תנן - השתא סבור דתקצץ ממש, והיינו דקאמר כריסו נבקעת. ומשני: ה"ק, תקצץ ידו על טבורו, פי' על שנגע על טבורו, ולעולם לטותא הוא; והא דקתני כריסו נבקעת, לא קאי אתקצץ, אלא על ישב לו קוץ, דאם לא יסיר הקוץ תבקע כריסו. וקשה: דמאי ס"ד מעיקרא? דהא בהדיא קתני והלא כריסו נבקעת אחר ישב לו קוץ! ומיהו, בתוספתא גריס והלא כריסו נבקעת ברישא, והשתא אתי שפיר. ומ"מ משני דה"ק: אם אסור לעולם ליגע, פעמים שכריסו נבקעת, כגון אם ישב לו קוץ:
Tosafot on Niddah 13b:10:2.english: Evidently we learned [it as actual] law - Now [the Gemara] thought that [the hand] is literally severed, and that is why it says, "[Won't] his belly be split open?" And it answers: This is what it is saying: "His hand shall be severed upon his navel" — meaning, for touching upon his navel — and in truth it is a curse. And that which it teaches, "his belly will be split open," does not refer to "shall be severed," but rather to "a thorn was stuck in it," for if he does not remove the thorn, his belly will split open. And it is difficult: For what was [the Gemara's] initial thought? For behold, it explicitly teaches "and won't his belly be split open?" after "a thorn was stuck in it"! However, in the Tosefta the text reads "and won't his belly be split open?" at the beginning, and now it works out well. And nevertheless, [the Gemara] answers that this is what it is saying: If it is forbidden ever to touch, there are times that his belly will be split open, such as if a thorn was stuck in it.

Tosafot on Niddah 13b:2:1.hebrew: המקשה עצמו לדעת יהא בנדוי - אינו מנודה מעצמו, אלא כלומר: חייבים לנדותו, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כח:): עד היכן הוא גלגול שבועה? עד שיאמר: השבע לי שאין עבדי אתה. ההוא שמותי משמתינן ליה, דתניא: הקורא לחברו עבד יהא בנדוי. משמע, דיהא בנדוי היינו דמשמתינן ליה:
Tosafot on Niddah 13b:2:1.english: One who intentionally causes himself an erection shall be in ostracism - He is not ostracized on his own, but rather it means: they are obligated to ostracize him. As we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (28b): "To what extent is the extension of an oath? Until he says: Swear to me that you are not my slave. That one, we excommunicate him, for it is taught: One who calls his fellow a slave shall be in ostracism." This implies that "shall be in ostracism" means that we excommunicate him.

Tosafot on Niddah 13b:4:1.english: Whether by hand or by foot - This means that he rubs his member with [his] hand or with [his] foot.

Tosafot on Niddah 13b:5:1.hebrew: קשים גרים לישראל כספחת - מה שמקשה רש"י דלא חשיב בסוטה ערבות דערב רב, י"ל: לפי שלא ידע חשבונן. מיהו, במכילתא אמר דערב רב היו כפלים כיוצאי מצרים. ור"י מפרש, דלפיכך קשים, שמטמעים בישראל; ואמר בפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף ע:): אין שכינה שורה אלא על משפחות המיוחסות שבישראל. וכן נראה, דהתם על ההיא מילתא מייתי דר' חלבו: [וע"ע תוס' יבמות מז: ותוס' קדושין ע: ד"ה קשים]:
Tosafot on Niddah 13b:5:1.english: Converts are as difficult for Israel as a scab - As for what Rashi objects, that [the Gemara] in Sotah does not reckon the mutual guarantee of the mixed multitude, one can say: Because [the Gemara] did not know their count. However, in the Mekhilta it says that the mixed multitude was twice as many as those who left Egypt. And the Ri explains that they are difficult for this reason: because they become assimilated into Israel; and it says in the chapter "Asarah Yuchasin" (Kiddushin 70b): "The Divine Presence rests only upon families of distinguished lineage in Israel." And so it appears, for there [in Kiddushin], it cites [the statement] of Rabbi Ḥelbo in connection to that matter. [And see further Tosafot, Yevamot 47b, and Tosafot, Kiddushin 70b, s.v. Kashim.]

Tosafot on Niddah 13b:7:1.hebrew: עד שיכלו כל הנשמות שבגוף - והא דאמר (שבת דף קיח:): אילמלי שמרו ישראל ב' שבתות, מיד היו נגאלים — וי"ל, דהרבה היו יולדות בכרס אחד:
Tosafot on Niddah 13b:7:1.english: Until all the souls in the Guf are finished - And as for that which [the Gemara] says (Shabbat 118b): "If Israel kept two Shabbats, they would immediately be redeemed" — one can say that [women] would give birth to many [children] in a single womb.
